extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of electric utilities and independent power producers; environmental compliance staff, consultants, and P.E.s preparing facility evaluation reports for CCR management units
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for conducting facility evaluations to identify and delineate Coal Combustion Residuals Management Units (CCRMU) and preparing Part 1 and Part 2 Facility Evaluation Reports (FERs) under the CCR rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner/Operator liability and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's revision to the definition of Operator follows standard 'operator' liability under environmental regulations; because multiple entities may potentially be liable (i.e., owners and operators), as long as one responsible entity (an owner or operator) has complied with the requirements, EPA will consider the obligation satisfied as to all potentially liable parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with EPA's typical practice (see 45 FR 33295 (May 19, 1980)), EPA will initially rely on owners and operators to determine among themselves how best to ensure compliance. EPA has finalized the revisions to Owner and Operator as proposed without revision (codified at §257.53).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of regulated facilities (covered facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing amendments to regulate CCRMU at all active electric utilities or independent power producers that generated power for the electrical grid on or after October 19, 2015, in addition to those facilities with legacy CCR surface impoundments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facilities are referred to as 'covered facilities.' EPA considered but declined to expand regulation to unknown/unidentified inactive facilities without legacy CCR surface impoundments because of unknown extent; EPA also explains why identified 'Other Active Facilities' with CCRMU should be included for regulatory consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility evaluation purpose and identification threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the facility evaluation is to confirm whether any CCRMU exist on-site and, if so, to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of the unit(s). The facility evaluation must identify any CCRMU containing one ton or more of CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FER must also identify CCRMU containing between one and 1,000 tons (regulation of those units is deferred until permitting). EPA relied on RCRA subtitle C Facility Assessment and CERCLA all appropriate inquiry (Phase I/II) processes in developing these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step Facility Evaluation process (Part 1 and Part 2 FERs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility evaluation is a two-step process: Part 1 consists of a thorough review of available records (information collection and data gap identification); Part 2 consists of a physical facility inspection and any necessary field work to fill data gaps and verify locations/boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded that creating two separate reports—one for each step—is consistent with established RCRA/CERCLA approaches, reduces rework and burden, and increases transparency by allowing public review of the Part 1 work plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection requirements (Part 1 FER content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 1 FER must gather and review all reasonably and readily available information regarding past and present placement (including spilled/released CCR left on the ground) to identify potential CCRMU locations, preliminary boundaries, lateral and vertical dimensions, and estimates of volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects facilities to search records reasonably and readily available to the facility. Useful documents include inspection reports; history of construction reports; fugitive dust control plans; annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action reports; ASDs; ACM and other corrective action reports; closure plans/reports; permits and permit applications (NPDES, solid waste, dam safety, air permits); historical and contemporary monitoring and reporting data; operating logs and maps; historical aerial photographs, site photographs, topographic maps, and engineering/construction drawings. The agency expects the facility to be able to identify date, locations, durations, and volumes/estimated quantities of CCR placement by the conclusion of the evaluation where information exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of data gaps and remedy plan (Part 1 requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Part 1 FER must include a narrative that documents the data reviewed, lists all data and information indicating the presence or absence of CCRMU, identifies any data gaps, and provides a plan for remedying identified data gaps through a physical examination of the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must include major milestones needed to fill each identified data gap (e.g., physical examination, sampling of media, measurements of CCR concentrations or physical presence, delineation of CCRMU) and dates to complete the needed tasks. Updates to data gap remedy plans must be added to the public record during FER Part 1 as necessary and timely. Part 1 must include a P.E. certification that the FER meets §257.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical site inspection and field work (Part 2 requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 2 requires a visual inspection of the entire facility to look for evidence of CCR placement on the land; at a minimum a visual inspection to confirm Part 1 information and identify anomalies that warrant further investigation. Where necessary, physical inspection must include field investigation activities (e.g., exploratory soil borings, geophysical assessments, soil sampling) to establish locations and boundaries and to determine whether potential areas contain at least one ton of CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities may inspect by walking, motorized vehicles, or drone footage. The extent of inspection and fieldwork depends on the quality/quantity of records; sparse records require more extensive inspection. EPA recommends sampling be conducted using standard industry methods (including relevant State standards). The FER must discuss quality assurance procedures, sampling equipment handling, sample collection, analytical methods, and data reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 2 FER content and narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 2 FER must include specified elements documenting findings from the physical evaluation and how data gaps were addressed, including location, size, physical/engineering properties, evidence of spills/releases, structural instability, groundwater contamination, types of CCR, closure activities, and supporting information used to identify and assess CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to enumerated items (location on USGS/topographic maps, unit name/ID, purpose of CCRMU, foundation/abutment description, evidence of spills/releases and remediation, structural instability, groundwater contamination, size and volume estimates, CCR types, closure descriptions, lists of reviewed data), Part 2 must include a narrative documenting the nature and extent of field oversight activities and how each data gap identified in Part 1 was addressed. Part 2 must include a P.E. certification per §257.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: FER certification requirements (P.E. and owner/operator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both FER Part 1 and Part 2 are required to include a certification from a Professional Engineer (P.E.) stating that the FER meets the requirements at §257.75(c), and a certification to be signed by the owner or operator or an authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA requires a P.E. review of documents and that the P.E. sign the FER. Commenters raised concerns about subjectivity/technical precision for a P.E., but EPA finalized the certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER recordkeeping, submittal, and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Part 1 and Part 2 of the FER must be placed in the facility operating record, submitted to the appropriate regulating entity, and published on the facility's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: place in operating record (§257.105(f)(25)), submit to appropriate regulating entity (§257.106(f)(24)), and publish on the facility website (§257.107(f)(24)). This requirement supports transparency and public accessibility of evaluation findings and data gap plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement for widespread sampling if no evidence is found
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after a thorough document review (Part 1) and a visual inspection (Part 2), the facility finds no evidence of any CCRMU containing one ton or more, no further testing or sampling is required to conclude that no such CCRMU are present at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explicitly states it is not requiring facilities to conduct widespread site sampling to prove absence of CCRMU; all recorded observations and data gathered must be assembled and incorporated into the FER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations regarding use of RCRA/CERCLA processes and investigative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA relied heavily on investigation processes under the current RCRA and CERCLA programs (RCRA subtitle C Facility Assessment and CERCLA all appropriate inquiry Phase I/II) in developing the facility evaluation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concurs that separate reporting for information review and physical evaluation aligns with these established approaches, and provides illustrative examples of information sources and investigative indicators (e.g., aerial photos, groundwater monitoring reports indicating CCRMU contributions, permit documents, topographic changes suggesting ponds/dams). EPA also notes that interviews of current/former personnel are not required but are recommended when feasible to assist identification of data and information.
